subject: Lumos Health RFP: PHI scoping, de-id playbook and BAA exhibit
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <procurement@lumoshealth.com>

Cc: it-security@lumoshealth.com; legal@lumoshealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFP Clarification: PHI scoping and BAA exhibit request

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the initial response to our RFP. A couple of items we need clarified to move to vendor evaluation:

1) We need a succinct description of where PHI may be present in transit and at rest when using your hosted API and when using a private deployment in our VPC. Diagrams are helpful.
2) Please provide your de-identification approach for text inputs that may contain PHI (examples: name, MRN, provider notes). Is there an automated de-id pipeline you offer or recommended patterns?
3) On the BAA exhibit, our legal team flagged subcontractor disclosure and the cache retention clause — we require a proposed exhibit showing you acknowledge responsibility for downstream subprocessors and a maximum ephemeral cache TTL for model KV caches for hosted deployments.

Can we get these items by EOD tomorrow? We plan to shortlist vendors next week.

Best,
Sasha
Sasha Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager, Lumos Health

Subject: Re: RFP Clarification: PHI scoping and BAA exhibit request

Hi Sasha — thank you, and great questions. Circling in Ben (product security) and Monica (legal ops) to provide the artifacts. High-level answers below; I’ll attach the diagrams and a draft BAA exhibit in a follow-up within the timeline.

Short answers:
- PHI scope and flow: For Redwood Hosted API, PHI can appear in the request body (text inputs) and will be held in-memory on inference nodes during request processing; we persist only audit logs and short-lived metrics (no raw request storage by default). For Redwood Private (VPC), PHI stays in your network and our control plane only exchanges job scheduling metadata; customers can opt for on-prem inference where no traffic leaves their environment.
- De-identification: We maintain a documented de-id playbook and provide an optional pre-processing microservice (deid-agent) that performs configurable named-entity redaction and token masking before requests reach the model. We recommend token-level redaction + synthetic identifier replacement for PII/PHI fields in higher-risk workflows.
- Subprocessors & cache TTL: We accept responsibility for subprocessors we engage and include them in the applicable BAA exhibit; for hosted deployments, we propose a default KV cache TTL of 1 hour for PHI-tagged requests, configurable down to 0 (no caching) in the console.

Next steps: Ben will attach the dataflow diagram and technical notes; Monica will attach the de-id playbook and draft BAA exhibit with the subcontractor list and the cache TTL language.

Cheers,
Avery Johnson
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0173

Attachments (coming in separate email): redwood_hipaa_dataflow_diagram.pdf, redwood_deid_playbook_v1.2.docx, baa-exhibit-draft-2027-04-01.pdf

Subject: Re: RFP Clarification: PHI scoping and BAA exhibit request

Hi all — attaching the technical artifacts and callouts (see attachments). Summary of technical controls and evidence links:

- Hosted API flow: request -> edge ingress (TLS 1.3) -> auth/proxy -> inference pool node (GPU) -> KV cache (RAM, TTL) -> response. Persistent storage: audit events (events store), metrics (aggregated), model weights. We do not write raw request payloads to disk for hosted customers by default; customers can enable request logging for troubleshooting (opt-in).
- Private/VPC: control plane metadata (request id, model id) flows through our control plane; inference traffic is routed peer-to-peer over an encrypted tunnel or remains inside the customer VPC when Private On-Prem package is deployed.
- Encryption: data in transit TLS 1.3, at rest AES-256 for stored artifacts (S3), KMS key management options for customer-managed keys.
- De-id agent: containerized microservice that supports configurable NER models (open-source and vendor models), regex rules, and a plugin system for custom transformations. We versioned the deid playbook and include sample rule-sets for common PHI fields.
- Evidence: logs of recent SOC 2 review section, KMS certificate, and a sanitized sample of the audit log are linked in the shared drive.

Notes on cache TTL: To balance utility and safety, we recommend 1 hour default but will set TTL=0 for endpoints explicitly handling PHI. We can also offer a policy that automatically disables KV caching when an input is tagged PHI via the deid-agent.

-ben
Ben Carter
Product Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP Clarification: PHI scoping and BAA exhibit request

Hi Sasha and team — attaching the draft BAA exhibit as requested (baa-exhibit-draft-2027-04-01.pdf). Key legal points summarized below for quick review:

- Subprocessors: Redwood will list all subprocessors with roles and contact points in the exhibit; we accept liability for obligations that flow from the BAA to the extent permitted by law and will notify Lumos 30 days prior to onboarding material subprocessors. We include a subprocessor addendum template for streamlined updates.
- Data handling & obligations: For hosted services, Redwood will not retain PHI beyond necessary processing except for audit and aggregated metrics (retained for 90 days by default; retention windows configurable). For Private deployments, the exhibit clarifies that customer-controlled deployments retain PHI under customer policies.
- Cache & ephemeral data: Exhibit includes a clause limiting KV/in-memory cache TTL for PHI to a maximum of 1 hour unless otherwise agreed; customers can set TTL=0 for zero caching.
- Right to audit & breach notification: We include standard audit cooperation and 72-hour breach notification language; operational details for incident response are in the exhibit appendix.

Please review and let us know any edits. If your legal team prefers redlines, we can accept a tracked PDF or use DocuSign for an initial acknowledgment. Happy to set a short call tomorrow to walk through the exhibit.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: baa-exhibit-draft-2027-04-01.pdf
